questions.q: Why did the family have to leave their home?
choices: The mistress was ill and had to go to a warm country
The master had lost all his money in a bad bank
The house had burned down in a fire one night
The master had been given important work in London
questions.evidence: she must leave her home at once, and go to a warm country

questions.q: Who were Black Beauty and Ginger sold to?
choices: The master's old friend, the Earl of W----
Mr. Blomefield, the vicar of the parish
Mr. Clay, the master brick-maker
A horse dealer who sold horses in London
questions.evidence: Master had sold Ginger and me to his old friend, the Earl of W----

questions.q: What promise came with giving Merrylegs to the vicar?
choices: He should never be sold
He must be raced at the fair every year
He must be kept together with Ginger
He must be taken up to London with them
questions.evidence: it was on the condition that he should never be sold

questions.q: What kind of work did John decide he wanted to do next?
choices: Work with a first-rate colt-breaker and trainer
Drive a cab of his own on the streets of London
Take a small farm and grow wheat and barley
Go abroad with the master and mistress

questions.q: Why did John want to train young horses?
choices: To help them get a fair start instead of being spoiled
Because colt-breaking paid the very highest wages
Because he was tired of driving the family carriage
Because the master had told him it was what he must do

The master and mistress in the carriage
The footman with all the heavy luggage

To keep the horses from bolting
To give them a last handful of oats
To keep out of the cold wind

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The sad breaking-up of Beauty's happy home
Beauty's first long journey on a railway train
John buying a new young horse to train
A fire that broke out at the railway station
